$comment: Self-derived finetype drift contract for source.naics, checked by the in-engine finetype_validate@1 gate (the model-free `ft_validate` DuckDB table macro). ft_validate MELTS every column to VARCHAR, so this contract uses ONLY the string-surviving JSON-Schema keywords. ENFORCED: the `enum` closed domain on level; the `pattern` on code — finetype's canonical `identity.industry.naics` validation pattern, VERBATIM; and `minLength`/`maxLength` envelopes. That pattern used to be a local widening (`^[0-9]{2,6}(-[0-9]{2})?$`) because the canonical regex rejected the official hyphenated sector ranges 31-33, 44-45 and 48-49, which this dataset contains. finetype PR #74 taught the canonical pattern those three ranges, so the widening is not merely redundant — it is now STRICTLY MORE PERMISSIVE than the pattern it was written to compensate for, admitting 11-99, 77-88, 31-34 and any digit pair, plus 99, 00 and 0111. Note the hyphenated branch is an exhaustive literal alternation, not a general `(-[0-9]{2})?` suffix: Census publishes exactly three sector ranges (31-33 Manufacturing, 44-45 Retail Trade, 48-49 Transportation and Warehousing) and nothing else may wear that shape. Keeping this in lockstep with the canonical is the point — if the two ever diverge again, fix this file rather than widening it. NOT ENFORCED, by design: numeric ranges (a numeric `type` BACKFIRES to 100% reject once melted to VARCHAR); NULLs (invisible to ft_validate); and object-level `required` (documentation only). Free-text fields (title, description, corpus) carry LOOSE length envelopes with generous headroom (descriptions/corpus run to several KB), not tight formats. Derived from build/naics.parquet: a pass-through on today's 2,125 rows, a fail-closed tripwire for future drift (an unknown level, a malformed code).
